text: Billene Seyoum Woldeyes (Amharic: ቢለኔ ሥዩም ወልደየስ; born 1982) is an Ethiopian politician, poet, and author who has served as the Foreign Press Secretary for the Office of the Prime Minister of Ethiopia since 5 November 2018. She speaks as the prime minister's foreign spokesperson in English. Billene was born in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and is the last of three children with two brothers. She moved to Harare, Zimbabwe at a young age before relocating to Canada and then returning to Ethiopia. In her book, she reflects on her multinational upbringing, stating, "I have spent half of my life outside of my birth country Ethiopia. Nevertheless, some norms of Ethiopiawinet (Ethiopianess) injected in me through socialization have sustained themselves throughout the years." After completing high school in Harare, she pursued two years of college in Marketing Management at the Addis Ababa University, College of Commerce. She then studied International Relations at the University of British Columbia, Vancouver from 2004 to 2008. She earned an MA in Gender and Peacebuilding from the University for Peace and another MA in Peace, Security, Development and International Conflict Transformation at the University of Innsbruck, Austria. Billene returned to Addis Ababa at the end of 2010 and began her career there. In 2010, three weeks after returning, she launched her blog EthiopianFeminism, which she renamed to AfricanFeminism in 2012. AfricanFeminism is a digital African feminist platform that shares works of feminist African writers and encourages dialogue, with the stated purpose of "to understand similar issues on the continent and engage with other African feminists. It was also a response to the lack of Ethiopian voices on continental issues." In 2011, she co-founded the spoken-word poetry collective Zemneged-Andinet (meaning "from a place of unity" in Amharic), which included both English and Amharic writing poets who believed in words as a medium of artistic expression, and performed in venues in Addis Ababa. From 2011 to 2013, she served as the Deputy Training Lead at the Institute of Peace and Security Studies – Africa Peace and Security Program in Addis Ababa. In 2013, she became president of Ethiopia's Association of Women in Business (AWiB). In 2014, she published her book, Transformative Spaces: Enabling Authentic Female Leadership Through Self Transformation. The Case of AWiB. Since 2010, she has contributed to multiple newsletters, including Pambazuka News, on topics related to women and girls' rights, and has also served as an editor for the Association for Women's Sanctuary and Development (AWSAD)'s newsletter. She worked as a consultant on the Agricultural Growth Program-Agribusiness and Market Development (AGP-AMDe) project of ACDI-VOCA, focusing on content development and management to enhance the capacity of Ethiopian small-scale farmers. In 2016, she was selected as an Acumen East African Fellow. Billene is the founder of the social impact company Earuyan Solutions. She was one of the originators of the 50-50 gender balance concept for Ethiopian government. In an open letter addressed to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, published by The Reporter, Billene Seyoum Weldeyes and Sewit Hailesellasie Tadesse recommended a 50-50 gender balance in the ministerial cabinet, Prime Minister's gender advisory group, CSO Law, the Women's Rights Defenders Forum, and other institutions to strengthen the Prime Minister's commitment to gender equality and justice. Prime Minister Ahmed responded positively and appointed 10 female ministers when forming his cabinet on 16 October 2018. Billene was then appointed as the Press Secretary for the Office of the Prime Minister of Ethiopia in November 2018, following the end of the Government Communication Affairs Office (GCAO). Multiple platforms have noted her preference for not being addressed with the title Weizero or Weizerit (roughly translated to Mrs. or Miss.). False information circulated around 1 January 2019 claiming she had been fired and replaced by Nigussie Tilahun, but Billene remained the press secretary in charge of English and digital media; Nigussie Tilahun joined the secretariat as press secretary to assist with the Amharic section. She is an author of several poems, including Things I Imagine Telling My Daughter, Make It Happen, From Foetus to Woman, and others.
